t: That the following sums are appropriated, out of any money in the, Treasury not otherwise appropriated, for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1972, for public works for water and power development, including the Corps of Engineers—Civil, the Bureau of Reclamation, the Bonneville Power Administration and other power agencies of the Department of the Interior, the Appalachian Regional Commission, the Federal Power Commission, the Tennessee Valley Authority, the Atomic Energy Commission, and related independent agencies and commissions, and for other purposes, namely

fable.w: This is an appropriations enacting clause that only lists the agencies and commissions receiving funds for fiscal year 1972. The tempting reading is that the named "commissions" (e.g. the Appalachian Regional Commission) signal an advisory body with outside members, but they appear only as funding recipients. The section sets out no consultation, hearing, comment, rulemaking, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government.
fable.s: the Appalachian Regional Commission, the Federal Power Commission, the Tennessee Valley Authority, the Atomic Energy Commission, and related independent agencies and commissions

qwen_block.w: This section is a standard appropriations clause that authorizes the spending of federal funds for various government agencies and projects. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or private entities) before a decision is made. It merely lists the entities receiving funding.
qwen_block.s: That the following sums are appropriated, out of any money in the, Treasury not otherwise appropriated, for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1972, for public works for water and power development, including the Corps of Engineers—Civil, the Bureau of Reclamation, the Bonneville Power Administration and other power agencies of the Department of the Interior, the Appalachian Regional Commission, the Federal Power Commission, the Tennessee Valley Authority, the Atomic Energy Commission, and related independent agencies and commissions, and for other purposes, namely

opus.w: This is boilerplate appropriations language listing the agencies and purposes that will receive funding for fiscal year 1972. It creates no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. Mentioning the Appalachian Regional Commission, which has state members, only identifies who receives the money. It does not require any outside party to take part in a federal decision.
opus.s: That the following sums are appropriated, out of any money in the, Treasury not otherwise appropriated, for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1972, for public works for water and power development
opus.b:
This is the opening clause of an appropriations act. It names agencies that will receive funds and creates no process for outsiders to take part in a federal decision.

**Tempting but wrong reading:** The clause names the Appalachian Regional Commission, a federal-state body that includes state governors, so it might look like it brings outside parties into decisions. But the Commission appears here only as a recipient of funds. The clause sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period or right to sue, so the outside-party test is never met.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriations clause that authorizes funding for various federal agencies and projects. It does not contain any language requiring or recommending consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, the public, or private organizations). The entities listed are all federal agencies or commissions, making this internal government administration rather than public participation.
qwen_chat.s: That the following sums are appropriated, out of any money in the, Treasury not otherwise appropriated, for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1972, for public works for water and power development, including the Corps of Engineers—Civil, the Bureau of Reclamation, the Bonneville Power Administration and other power agencies of the Department of the Interior, the Appalachian Regional Commission, the Federal Power Commission, the Tennessee Valley Authority, the Atomic Energy Commission, and related independent agencies and commissions, and for other purposes, namely
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: The text lists various agencies and commissions, which might imply some form of coordination or participation among them.
Resolution: This is merely an appropriations clause listing the entities for which funds are being appropriated. It does not establish any process for outside parties to participate in decision-making, nor does it require consultation with non-federal entities. It is purely internal budgetary authorization.
